methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Drones & Autonomous (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 5 same-sector peers exist in Drones & Autonomous, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Airship Industries is a pre-seed stage company operating in the Drones & Autonomous sector. The comparable universe consists of six private companies in the same sector, including Zipline, Joby Aviation, Nuro, Archer Aviation, and Elroy Air. No public comparables exist in this narrow segment.

Peer-median valuation analysis is not applicable to Airship Industries. The screening identified five same-sector peers, but none satisfied the filtering criteria for stage-alignment, adjacent-stage proximity, or valuation-tier similarity required to establish a minimum of three datapoints for triangulation. Relying on an all-sector median would introduce material noise and obscure sector-specific dynamics at this early stage, making the method unsuitable for this analysis.

Without a sufficiently tight comparable set and absent alternative quantitative methods applied to the data provided, a defensible valuation range cannot be derived. The analysis reveals a critical constraint: pre-seed companies in emerging autonomous systems sectors often lack sufficient peer visibility at equivalent stages to support conventional comparable-company approaches. Any valuation estimate would require supplementary methodologies—such as founder background assessment, technology IP evaluation, or market-sizing frameworks—not present in the current dataset. Further data collection on the target's fundraising trajectory and the financial profiles of the identified peer set would be necessary to complete a triangulated valuation.
